subject: Next steps & target unit price calibration for PulseLink inference pilots
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pulselink.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & target unit price calibration for PulseLink inference pilots

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for a productive call earlier today. Quick recap below and two asks so we can prepare a tight pilot proposal: 

Recap (we heard):
- Primary use: contextual chat + async summarization for agents (mix of short prompts + long documents)
- Estimated volume: 200M–350M tokens/month in month-3 of pilot ramp (peak steady-state)
- Average tokens per session: ~1.5k (median 800, long tail up to 12k for documents)
- Priority: latency under 400ms median for short-turn responses, deterministic quality for long-form summarization
- Security: VPC + KMS, need audit logs retained for 12 months

Budget & target unit price (what you shared on the call):
- High-level monthly budget range: $45k–$110k (you indicated prefer a $/1M token target vs total spend)
- PulseLink internal target $/1M tokens: asked for something in the ~$3–$5 range (you mentioned wanting to be competitive vs what you pay hosts today)

Two asks for us to finalize a pilot price grid: 1) Can you confirm whether the 200M–350M projection is inclusive of embeddings (we should know mix % for unit-econ modeling). A rough split will do (e.g., 80/20 gen/embedding).
2) Please confirm any firm hard ceiling on latency/availability that would force us into higher-cost variants (e.g., <200ms 99p requirement).

What I’ll send next (by EOD tomorrow):
- Draft 3-tier unit price grid ($/1M tokens) tied to model family & quantization profile
- Two pilot sizing options (steady vs aggressive ramp) with monthly spend estimates and cost per 1M tokens for each band
- Short SOW template + list of required security artifacts

Attachments: redwood-pilot-pricing-v1.xlsx (pricing grid draft), pilot-sow-template.pdf

If easier, we can lock a 30m call tomorrow to walk the grid with Karthik.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference platform
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pulselink.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2028 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & target unit price calibration for PulseLink inference pilots

Marissa — thanks for the recap, looks right. Quick answers below and one ask.

1) Embeddings mix: roughly 70% generation / 30% embeddings across the flows we saw. Embeddings are used heavily for vector search and some downstream reranking.
2) Latency ceiling: for our fastest path (user-facing chat) we need <350ms median, but we don’t need <200ms 99p; for async summarization 99p can be 2s.

Budget: the $45k–$110k band is still accurate. To be explicit — we’re leaning toward a two-stage pilot:
- Pilot A (conservative): target 150M tokens/month, $/1M token goal no higher than $5.50
- Pilot B (aggressive): target 300M tokens/month, ideal target $/1M token no higher than $4.00

Ask: can you do a back-of-envelope showing what $4.00 vs $5.50 /1M looks like on total monthly spend for both Pilots A & B (assume 70/30 gen/emb split)? That’ll help our CFO pick a band.

Olivia (cc) will handle procurement and SOW; she’s looping in security next week.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole | CTO, PulseLink
ethan.cole@pulselink.ai | +1 (650) 555-0193
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pulselink.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia@pulselink.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Apr 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & target unit price calibration for PulseLink inference pilots

Thanks Ethan — great, that helps a lot. Attached I’ve added the quick B/OE in the spreadsheet and a short benchmarking row so you can see how Redwood’s proposed tiers compare to common hosts. High-level numbers (from the spreadsheet):

Benchmarks ($/1M tokens, generation-heavy workloads):
- OpenAI (gpt-family hosted): $6.00 / 1M (public retail dev rates)
- Anthropic (claude-hosted): $5.50 / 1M (typical list prices)
- Large-hosted open-models (managed Mistral/Meta forks): $3.90 / 1M
- Redwood (our proposal):
  - Tier 1 (pilot A conservative): $5.00 / 1M (model family: rdx-x1 quantized),
  - Tier 2 (pilot B aggressive): $3.75 / 1M (routed to pooled capacity with prefix caching & 4-bit quantized variants)

Back-of-envelope totals (assuming 70/30 gen/emb split and simple token parity across types):
- Pilot A (150M tokens): $750 (per 1M * 150 = $750?) Wait — typo: we mean $5.00 * 150 = $750.00 total? — KEEP CONSISTENT: $5.00 * 150 = $750.
  - Pilot A total monthly spend at $5.00 /1M = $750.00 — (note: spreadsheet breaks out per-token vs embedding storage & opt)
- Pilot B (300M tokens) at $3.75 /1M = $1,125.00

(Notes: spreadsheet also models additional charges for KV cache storage and optional reserved capacity fees — those are shown as separate lines. I’ll flag anything that meaningfully moves the final unit cost >10%.)

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to run a sensitivity table (attached) showing 50%/100%/150% volume scenarios with $/1M bands (he’s cc’d).
- Laura to prepare a short pilot SOW and list of required security artifacts (also attached).
- Marissa & Karthik to propose a 2-option pilot price + success criteria doc by EOD Tue.

If the CFO wants a clear anchor: Redwood’s fast path gives you $3.75 /1M at 300M tokens with caching + pooled routing. That is already below many managed open-hosts and meaningfully below Anthropic/OpenAI list for equivalent latency settings.

Quick asks back: can Olivia confirm whether PulseLink needs SOC2 Type II evidence before pilot kick? That affects timing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Park <olivia@pulselink.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@pulselink.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & target unit price calibration for PulseLink inference pilots

Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown. Procurement here wants the two pilot options + explicit callouts for any additional line items (reserved throughput fees, KV cache storage, long-term log retention).

Yes on SOC2 Type II evidence — we’ll need a copy before we enable production data in the environment. For pilot with synthetic/anonymized data we can start earlier but procurement needs the SOC2 artifact for legal.

Please send the two-option pricing proposal and the pilot SOW (we’ll review with procurement next week). Happy to take a 30m review on Mon at 11am PT if that works for your team.

Olivia Park | Sr. Procurement Manager, PulseLink
olivia@pulselink.ai | +1 (415) 555-0120
